newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BOURSE QUIET, SHADOWED BY CZECH CROWN MOVES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BOURSE QUIET, SHADOWED BY CZECH CROWN MOVES.

text.p: Reecent sharp rises in Czech interest rates, impsed to shore up an ailing crown, restrained activity on the Slovak Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with volumes low and trading listless.
The 16-share SAX index, however, edged up 0.95 point to 196.29 points, on gains to average prices in commercial bank VUB and some other medium-size issues.
"Investors have been watching money markets and hedging their positions, rather than play on the bourse at the moment," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.
Steel maker VSZ dropped five crowns to 745 after holding stable for three weeks, on a volume of 298 shares, well below the volumes traded in the issue over this month.
"Concerning the (VSZ) price, I welcome this drop," Betko said. "Finally, a post-dividend weakening comes into effect, which indicates the share is on a normal, reasonable track."
The bank VUB closed unchanged at 1,530 with average prices 1.7 percent higher, but only 15 shares traded, and Betko said this was not enough to indicate a trend.
Overall volume rose to 180,080 shares, from 168,577 shares traded on Friday, while turnover increased to 276.96 million crowns, from 86.24 million.
